text: The suggested owner of an epic is the Template and Rules §R5.3 owner phrase that most of its stories carry, and the scope of an epic is the scope token inside its own ID (PLT, ITG, P1-P10, S1-S9). The Ownership Map is used to name each service, its schema, REST base, topic and task queue and its owned workflows, tables, operations and events; it does not name an epic owner, so it is not the source of the owner phrase.
why: The work package asks for one scope and one suggested owner per epic and says to use the Ownership Map for every owner, but the catalog holds the suggestion per story only and the map has no owner column, so the epic value must be derived from 1034 story rows.

text: The wave of an epic is the earliest wave carried by its stories. For a service epic the service's Arch v5 wave from the Ownership Map is shown beside it where the two differ, and the story-level conflict stays with the story work packages (§R5.6). RWB-ITG-NFR is at wave 1 because its two stories are wave-1 EP01-TE stories; the phrase 'Platform and NF' at wave 0 in §R5.6 is read as the NF-01 to NF-08 stories, which sit in the platform epics at wave 0.
why: The catalog gives one wave per epic and no rule for it, the stories of several service epics carry more than one wave, and the W-MAP table names 'NF' at wave 0 while the non-functional integration epic sits at wave 1.
